title: The melted chocolate bar that led to the microwave oven
hook: A melted candy bar in an engineer's pocket led to the microwave oven.
summary: Engineer Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar melting near a radar tube in 1945, tested popcorn and an egg, and Raytheon turned it into the first microwave oven, though he had never finished grammar school.
sources: Wikipedia: Percy Spencer. Raytheon engineer, 1945 magnetron observation, candy bar melting, popcorn test, little formal schooling.
Wikipedia: Microwave oven. Raytheon patent 1945, Radarange 1947 about 340 kg (750 lb) and about 1.8 m tall.
Smithsonian Magazine and Raytheon history on Percy Spencer and the Radarange.

lines.text: A melted chocolate bar led to the microwave oven.
In nineteen forty-five, engineer Percy Spencer was standing near a radar tube.
lines.caps: In *1945, | engineer *Percy Spencer | *stood near | a *radar tube

lines.text: The candy bar in his pocket turned to goo.
So he tried popcorn kernels, and they popped across the lab.
Next he tried an egg, which exploded.
Raytheon built the first oven two years later.
It was nearly six feet tall and weighed over seven hundred pounds.
Spencer had never even finished grammar school.
A war radar part now warms lunch in kitchens everywhere.

post.caption:
A snack melting in a pocket changed every kitchen on Earth.
What accidental invention do you use every day?
